δέδονται δὲ αὐτῷ παρὰ Θεοῦ καὶ Πα- τρὸς, ὡς Σωτῆρι καὶ Λυτρωτῇ καὶ Ζωοποιῷ, καὶ 86 καταφωτίζειν ἰσχύοντι, καὶ παντὸς ἀπαλλάττειν κα- κοῦ· ἀφίστησι δὲ αὐτοὺς
ὁλοτρόπως τῶν ἀρχαίων ἠθῶν, καὶ φρενοβλαβείας τῆς πρώτης. Ἔθος μὲν γὰρ τοῖς
τῶν εἰδώλων προσκυνηταῖς, τοὺς ἐκ τῶν δαιμο- 70.241 νίων χρησμοὺς ἀγαπᾷν, καὶ
κενολόγοις τισὶ νεκρο- μάντεσι προσκεῖσθαι φιλεῖν, οἳ λέγουσι μὲν ἀληθὲς οὐδέν·
ἀνερεύγονται δὲ ὥσπερ τὸ εἰς νοῦν ἧκον ἁπλῶς. Ἀλλ' ὑμεῖς, φησὶ, κἂν εἰ προσίοιτό

pass_a_gloss: [...] those who talk emptily, who sound from the belly; [is] not a nation toward its God? Why do they seek out the dead about the living? For he gave law for help, so that they may say: Not as this word, about which it is not possible to give gifts about it. Emmanuel himself weaves an instructive discourse for those who set hope in him, who were reckoned among children; and they have been given to him by God and Father, as to Saviour and Redeemer and Life-maker, and able to enlighten, and to free from every evil; and he removes them wholly from the ancient habits, and from the first madness. For it is a custom for the worshippers of the idols to love the oracles from the demons, and to love to cling to some empty-talking necromancers, who say nothing true; but they belch out as it were simply what came into mind. But you, he says, even if someone should come, saying: Seek those sounding from the earth, that is, those pretending to bring up the dead, and as from Hades to make the divinations; or the belly-talkers, who pretend to have some gods in the belly, and so to speak to those who come the things from those, do not admit the counsel. For they sound from their own belly alone, and they are not an understanding nation, so as both to seek out God and to learn something from him. And say to those counselling those things: Why do they seek out the dead about the living? Do you see how he makes [them] most sensible? For he orders not only to depart from the perversity and madness of those, but indeed he commands also to become good counsellors to those who have strayed. For say, he says: Why do they seek out the dead about the living? For common and human is the reasoning. For what sort of account would there be in wishing to question those lying in the earth, or souls perhaps come to be in Hades, about those still living? And in another manner too it is wholly ignorant to give heed to necromancies, and to the lies of the sorcerers who have the mind dead, and as it were a heart grown cold. For they do not know the creator of all, they do not have in themselves the life-making word of God. And they are besides this also caretakers of dead works. How then do the living, that is, those having in themselves the life-giving from above, and enriched with the living Word of God, ask the dead about themselves? Say these things then, he says, adding that he gave law for help, that is, the gospel one, so that those giving heed to it may say: Not as this word, about which it is not possible to give gifts about it. For they sell the lie, those speaking the things from their own heart alone; but the saving and true law of God, that i[s] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: “…who talk emptily, who speak from the belly. Should not a nation go to its God? Why do they seek the dead on behalf of the living? For He gave the Law as a help, so that they might say: Not like this word, for which there are no gifts to give” (Isaiah 8:19-20).

Emmanuel Himself weaves a discourse of instruction for those who have set their hope on Him, who were reckoned among the children and have been given to Him by God the Father (Isaiah 8:18), as to the Savior, Redeemer, and Life-giver, who is able to enlighten them and to free them from every evil. And He draws them wholly away from their ancient habits and their former madness. For it is the custom of idol worshipers to love the oracles of demons and to cling to certain empty-talking necromancers, who say nothing true but simply belch out whatever comes into their heads.

But you, He says, even if someone comes to you and says, “Seek those who speak from the earth,” that is, those who pretend to bring up the dead and to give divinations as if from Hades, or the ventriloquists, who pretend to have certain gods in their belly and so to tell those who come to them what those gods say, do not accept the advice. For they speak only from their own belly, and they are not an understanding nation, such as would seek God and learn something from Him. And say to those who give that advice, “Why do they seek the dead on behalf of the living?”

Do you see how He makes them most sensible? For He not only commands them to turn away from the perversity and madness of those people, but also directs them to become good counselors to those who have gone astray. For say, He tells them, “Why do they seek the dead on behalf of the living?” The reasoning is common sense and human. For what reason could there be in wanting to question those who lie in the earth, or souls that have perhaps come to be in Hades, about people who are still alive?

And in another way too it is utterly ignorant to give heed to necromancy and to the lies of sorcerers, who have a dead mind and, as it were, a heart grown cold. For they do not know the Creator of all; they do not have within them the life-giving Word of God. Besides this, they also busy themselves with dead works. How then can the living, that is, those who have within themselves the life-giving power from above and are rich in the living Word of God, ask the dead about themselves?

So say these things, He says, adding that “He gave the Law as a help,” that is, the Law of the Gospel, so that those who heed it may say: “Not like this word, for which there are no gifts to give.” For those who speak only from their own heart sell falsehood; but the saving and true Law of God, that is…
